catalog_quote: The canonical structure of syllables is (C)(r)V(Tone), where the initial consonant and tone are optional. ... For monosyllabic words, the syllable always appeared tone-bearing, even in natural speech. A monosyllable rarely, if ever, reduces down to an unstressed vowel. ... The case of polysyllabic words is different, with the vowel of the non-final syllables often being reduced and non-tone bearing. Many of the first syllables in such words are bound or unbound prefixes that perform various functions. In almost all cases the prefixes are non-tone bearing or have a 22 or 33 (Chao pitch scale) tone, perhaps a neutralization of the two falling mid-tones ... Four tones were identified ... The typology of this tonal system is unusual in that it contains four falling tones, with the two mid-tones overlapping in an interesting manner ... Syllables without a full vowel never appeared to be tone…

tone_statements.citation: Tetseo, Sekholu. 2025. The Phonetics and Phonology of Tone in Chokri. Ph.D. thesis, Department of Linguistics and Language Technology, Tezpur University (supervisor Amalesh Gope). xxi+211 pp. Shodhganga hdl:10603/658203.
tone_statements.quote: Chokri exhibits a register tone system, aligning more closely with African tone systems than with the contour tone systems characteristic of Southeast Asian languages. The study identifies four level tones: extra high, high, mid, and low and one contour tone: Mid- rising. ... Chokri speakers rely exclusively on fundamental frequency (F0) to distinguish tone, with no significant role played by phonation, duration, or intensity, reinforcing its classification as a purely pitch-driven tone language.
tone_statements.locator: Abstract, p. i; tone chapters 4-6 = pp. 80-178 per table of contents
tone_statements.summary: Five lexical tones (four level: extra-high, high, mid, low; one mid-rising contour), register-type system cued by F0 alone, plus grammatical (floating) tone marking person/aspect/mood and derivation; no word-stress statement.

tone_statements.quote: This paper explores f0 downtrend processes in Chokri, a Tibeto-Burman language spoken in Nagaland, India. Chokri manifests five lexical tones, comprising four level tones- extra high (EH), high (H), mid (M), low (L), and one contour tone- mid-rising (MR).
tone_statements.summary: Five lexical tones (EH, H, M, L level + mid-rising contour); sentence-level declination, final lowering (M only) and automatic downstep.

tone_statements.quote: Chokri, on the other hand, belongs to the Tibeto Burman language family, with a rich tonal inventory of five lexical tones (Gope et al., 2024; Tetseo et al., 2021). ... Chokri, on the other hand, shows a total absence of phrasal tones as it does not have boundary tones or pitch accents.
tone_statements.summary: Five lexical tones; intonation realised by register modification only (no pitch accents, no boundary tones); declination and restricted final lowering; focus by pitch lowering.

sources.citation: Gogoi, Tulika, Sekholu Tetseo & Amalesh Gope. 2023. The phonetics of downtrends in Chokri. Proceedings of the 20th International Congress of Phonetic Sciences (ICPhS 2023), Prague, 1628-1632 (paper 948).
sources.quote: 'Bielenberg and Nienu [12] report the presence of 39 consonants, six vowels, and four tones in the language. However, our study shows that the segmental phoneme inventory of Chokri consists of 33 consonants, 7 vowels, and 5 lexical tones (four level tones- Extra High, High, Mid, and Low, and a contour (mid-rising) tone)'. Paper is on sentence-level f0 declination/downstep/final lowering; no word-stress statement.
sources.note: Open ICPhS paper explicitly contrasting its 5-tone analysis with Bielenberg & Nienu 2001; sentence prosody only, confirms tonal coding.

sources.note: Takes Chokri as a five-lexical-tone system (citing Gope et al. 2024, Tetseo et al. 2021) and studies tone-intonation interaction: Chokri has no boundary tones or pitch accents (no phrasal tones), uses register raising/lowering for questions vs declaratives, pause and final lengthening for prosodic boundaries; declination in all-H and all-L sequences (linear), exponential decay + final lowering only in all-M sequences; in-situ focus marked by pitch lowering over the whole IP. Keywords include Downstep, Prosodic Focus, Prosodic Structure, Tone.
